levels.title: Counting and Early Number Sense
levels.description: Foundation number skills: counting, recognising and ordering numbers to 20

atomic_skills.title: Count objects to 10
atomic_skills.description: Count a set of up to 10 physical or pictured objects with one-to-one correspondence

error_signatures.description: Skips or double-counts objects
Does not understand cardinality — last number is not the total
error_signatures.example: After counting '1,2,3,4,5' cannot state there are 5 objects

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use touch-counting with physical objects. Reinforce cardinality by asking 'how many altogether?' after every count.

atomic_skills.title: Count objects to 20
atomic_skills.description: Count sets of up to 20 objects accurately

error_signatures.description: Errors at teen numbers (13/14 confusion)
Does not bridge from 10 to 11

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use ten-frames. Emphasise the structure of teen numbers as '10 and some more'.

atomic_skills.title: Recognise and write numerals 0–20
atomic_skills.description: Identify and write numerals 0 to 20 correctly

error_signatures.description: Reverses numerals (e.g. 6/9, 2/5)

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Provide numeral formation practice with verbal description of strokes.

atomic_skills.title: Order numbers to 20
atomic_skills.description: Place numbers in ascending and descending order on a number line

error_signatures.description: Confuses before/after on number line

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use a physical number line walk. Ask 'which comes next when counting forward?'

atomic_skills.title: Compare numbers using < > =
atomic_skills.description: Use comparison symbols to compare pairs of numbers to 20

error_signatures.description: Reverses < and >

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use 'hungry crocodile' analogy — the mouth always faces the bigger number.

atomic_skills.title: Understand tens and ones to 99
atomic_skills.description: Partition two-digit numbers into tens and ones using place value

error_signatures.description: Treats digits as separate units rather than place value
Confuses tens and ones columns

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use base-10 blocks. Build the number physically then record it.

levels.title: Addition Concepts
levels.description: Build conceptual understanding of addition as combining and counting on

atomic_skills.title: Add by counting all
atomic_skills.description: Combine two groups and count all objects to find the total

error_signatures.description: Miscounts combined group
Does not understand combining increases the total

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use two distinct groups of objects. Model combining physically before counting.

atomic_skills.title: Add by counting on
atomic_skills.description: Start from the larger number and count on to add efficiently

error_signatures.description: Counts on from the first rather than larger number
Off-by-one error when counting on

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use a number line. Mark the starting number and physically jump the correct number of spaces.

atomic_skills.title: Doubles and near-doubles
atomic_skills.description: Know doubles to 10+10 and use them to calculate near-doubles

error_signatures.description: Does not apply double as a reference

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Teach doubles as a family. For near-doubles, explicitly show: 6+7 = 6+6+1 = 12+1.

atomic_skills.title: Make 10 strategy
atomic_skills.description: Bridge through 10 to add numbers crossing the tens boundary

error_signatures.description: Does not recognise bonds to 10
error_signatures.example: Cannot identify that 7 needs 3 to make 10

error_signatures.description: Does not split the second addend to bridge 10

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use ten-frames. Physically fill the frame to 10, then count remaining dots.

atomic_skills.title: Add two-digit numbers without regrouping
atomic_skills.description: Add two-digit numbers where ones do not cross ten

error_signatures.description: Adds digits without regard to place value
Does not partition into tens and ones

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use base-10 blocks. Separate tens and ones physically before adding.

atomic_skills.title: Add two-digit numbers with regrouping
atomic_skills.description: Add two-digit numbers that require carrying (regrouping ones into tens)

error_signatures.description: Adds ones correctly but forgets to carry
Does not understand regrouping means exchanging 10 ones for 1 ten
error_signatures.example: Groups 13 ones but writes 13 in the ones column

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use base-10 blocks to physically exchange 10 ones for a tens rod. Record each exchange step.

levels.title: Subtraction Concepts
levels.description: Subtraction as take away, difference, and inverse of addition

atomic_skills.title: Subtract by taking away
atomic_skills.description: Remove objects from a group and count what remains

error_signatures.description: Counts removed objects rather than remaining
error_signatures.example: 12-5: counts the 5 removed and says the answer is 5

error_signatures.description: Miscounts remaining objects

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Physically remove and cover the subtracted objects. Count only what remains uncovered.

atomic_skills.title: Subtraction by counting back
atomic_skills.description: Count back on a number line to subtract efficiently

error_signatures.description: Off-by-one error counting back
error_signatures.example: 15-4: starts at 15 and counts '15,14,13,12' but says 12 not 11

error_signatures.description: Counts back from the wrong number
error_signatures.example: Starts from the subtrahend rather than minuend

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Mark start and jumps on a number line. Count jumps, not landings.

atomic_skills.title: Find the difference by counting up
atomic_skills.description: Determine how many more by counting up from smaller to larger number

error_signatures.description: Confuses take-away with difference interpretation
error_signatures.example: Uses take-away method when difference is needed

error_signatures.description: Does not recognise subtraction as inverse of addition

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use a bar model showing two quantities. The difference is the gap between them.

atomic_skills.title: Subtract two-digit numbers without regrouping
atomic_skills.description: Subtract two-digit numbers where ones do not require borrowing

error_signatures.description: Subtracts smaller digit from larger regardless of position

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use base-10 blocks. Partition both numbers before subtracting column by column.

atomic_skills.title: Subtract two-digit numbers with regrouping
atomic_skills.description: Subtract using decomposition (borrowing) when ones column requires it

error_signatures.description: Forgets to reduce tens after borrowing
error_signatures.example: 43-18: borrows but still uses 4 tens giving 35

error_signatures.description: Does not understand borrowing as exchanging 1 ten for 10 ones
error_signatures.example: Tries to borrow from an empty column

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Physically exchange a tens rod for 10 ones. Record the exchange in the algorithm.

levels.title: Addition and Subtraction Fluency
levels.description: Build fluency with mental strategies and standard algorithms

atomic_skills.title: Compensation strategy for addition
atomic_skills.description: Round to a friendly number, add, then adjust

error_signatures.description: Rounds but forgets to compensate
error_signatures.example: 49+23: rounds 49 to 50, adds to get 73, forgets to subtract 1

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Explicitly record the round-add-adjust steps. Use a number line to show the adjustment.

atomic_skills.title: Splitting strategy for addition
atomic_skills.description: Partition both numbers into hundreds, tens, ones then add each part

error_signatures.description: Splits correctly but makes arithmetic error in partial sum

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use a written split layout. Record each partial sum clearly before combining.

atomic_skills.title: Compensation strategy for subtraction
atomic_skills.description: Round the subtrahend to a friendly number, subtract, then adjust

error_signatures.description: Adjusts in wrong direction after rounding subtrahend
error_signatures.example: 84-39: subtracts 40 getting 44, then subtracts 1 instead of adding 1

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use a number line. Show that subtracting 40 goes too far and must jump back 1.

atomic_skills.title: Add and subtract three-digit numbers
atomic_skills.description: Apply standard algorithm to three-digit addition and subtraction with regrouping

error_signatures.description: Multiple regrouping errors in algorithm
error_signatures.example: Correctly regroups ones but forgets second regroup in tens

error_signatures.description: Applies algorithm mechanically without checking reasonableness
error_signatures.example: Gets answer smaller than minuend in subtraction

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Estimate first to establish a benchmark. Check algorithm answer against estimate.

levels.title: Multiplication Concepts
levels.description: Introduction to multiplication as equal groups and arrays

atomic_skills.title: Identify and make equal groups
atomic_skills.description: Recognise and create equal groups; express as repeated addition

error_signatures.description: Does not understand groups must be equal
Confuses number of groups with group size
error_signatures.example: For 3 groups of 4 writes 4 × 3 but means 3 groups not 4

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use physical objects arranged into equal groups. Count groups first, then count in each group.

atomic_skills.title: Represent multiplication with arrays
atomic_skills.description: Create and interpret rectangular arrays; connect to multiplication notation

error_signatures.description: Confuses rows and columns
error_signatures.example: 3×4 array drawn as 4 rows of 3 and claimed to be different from 3 rows of 4

error_signatures.description: Does not connect array to multiplication equation
error_signatures.example: Cannot write 3×4=12 from a 3 by 4 array

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Label rows and columns explicitly. Show commutativity by rotating the array.

atomic_skills.title: Skip count by 2s, 5s, and 10s
atomic_skills.description: Count in multiples of 2, 5, and 10 to support multiplication understanding

error_signatures.description: Breaks pattern in skip counting

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use a hundreds chart and highlight multiples. Clap or step on multiples.

atomic_skills.title: Times tables: 2, 5, 10
atomic_skills.description: Recall and apply 2, 5, and 10 times tables with fluency

error_signatures.description: Off-by-one in table sequence

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Connect to skip counting. Visualise with arrays or number lines.

atomic_skills.title: Times tables: 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9
atomic_skills.description: Recall and apply remaining times tables with fluency

error_signatures.description: Confuses adjacent table facts
Cannot derive unknown fact from known facts

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Teach derivation strategies: use known facts as anchors. 6×8 = 5×8 + 8.

atomic_skills.title: Commutative property of multiplication
atomic_skills.description: Understand and apply a×b = b×a to reduce memorisation load

error_signatures.description: Believes order matters in multiplication

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Rotate an array physically. Count to confirm same total.

levels.title: Multiplicative Reasoning
levels.description: Apply and extend multiplication concepts including scaling and multi-digit

atomic_skills.title: Interpret multiplication as scaling
atomic_skills.description: Understand multiplication as making something n times as large

error_signatures.description: Confuses scaling with repeated addition only
error_signatures.example: Cannot represent 3 times as long on a diagram

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use tape diagrams (bar models) to show scaling. Draw and label n copies of the unit.

atomic_skills.title: Multiply 2-digit by 1-digit using splitting
atomic_skills.description: Apply distributive property: split tens and ones, multiply each part, recombine

error_signatures.description: Splits number but adds rather than multiplies parts
Partial product arithmetic error

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use an area model (grid). Label each section with its partial product.

atomic_skills.title: Multiply 3-digit by 1-digit
atomic_skills.description: Extend splitting strategy to hundreds, tens, and ones

error_signatures.description: Error in hundreds partial product
Forgets to include hundreds in the split

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use a 3-column area model. Ensure all three columns are multiplied.

atomic_skills.title: Multiply 2-digit by 2-digit
atomic_skills.description: Apply full area model or standard algorithm to 2-digit by 2-digit multiplication

error_signatures.description: Only multiplies ones by ones and tens by tens, ignoring cross products
Misaligns rows in standard algorithm
error_signatures.example: Second partial product not shifted left

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use a 2×2 area model (four cells). All four products must be found and summed.

atomic_skills.title: Apply distributive property
atomic_skills.description: Use a(b+c) = ab+ac to simplify multiplication calculations

error_signatures.description: Distributes only to first term

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use an area model. Show that the multiplier covers both parts of the split.

levels.title: Division Concepts
levels.description: Division as sharing, grouping, and as inverse of multiplication

atomic_skills.title: Division as equal sharing
atomic_skills.description: Share a quantity equally among groups; interpret remainder

error_signatures.description: Confuses divisor with quotient
error_signatures.example: 24÷6: says answer is 6 because there are 6 groups

error_signatures.description: Does not distribute equally — some groups larger

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use physical objects. Share one at a time into equal piles and count the result.

atomic_skills.title: Division as grouping
atomic_skills.description: Find how many equal groups can be made from a total

error_signatures.description: Confuses sharing and grouping interpretation
error_signatures.example: Uses sharing method when grouping is required

error_signatures.description: Does not connect grouping division to multiplication

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Act out: 'How many bags of 5 can I make from 20 apples?' Count groups made.

atomic_skills.title: Use multiplication to solve division
atomic_skills.description: Recognise division as the inverse of multiplication and use fact families

error_signatures.description: Does not recognise inverse relationship

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Build fact families: 4×6=24, 6×4=24, 24÷4=6, 24÷6=4. Show all four together.

atomic_skills.title: Divide 2-digit by 1-digit with remainder
atomic_skills.description: Apply short division; interpret and use remainders contextually

error_signatures.description: Does not bring down correctly in short division
error_signatures.example: Forgets to include remainder in next step

error_signatures.description: Cannot interpret remainder in context
error_signatures.example: Gets 3 remainder 2 but cannot explain what the 2 means

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use chunking (repeated subtraction) alongside short division. Map each step of chunking to short division.

levels.title: Fractions — Introduction
levels.description: Understand fractions as equal parts of a whole and on a number line

atomic_skills.title: Identify unit fractions
atomic_skills.description: Identify 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5, 1/8, 1/10 as equal parts of a whole

error_signatures.description: Does not require parts to be equal
Confuses numerator and denominator meaning
error_signatures.example: Says 1/4 means 1 out of 4 but interprets denominator as 'number of shaded parts'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Always fold or cut physical shapes. Confirm equality by overlapping parts.

atomic_skills.title: Identify non-unit fractions
atomic_skills.description: Name and write fractions with numerators greater than 1

error_signatures.description: Counts unshaded rather than shaded parts for numerator

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Explicitly circle shaded parts and count. Label numerator first, then denominator.

atomic_skills.title: Place fractions on a number line
atomic_skills.description: Mark and identify fractions between 0 and 1 on a number line

error_signatures.description: Does not divide the number line into equal parts
error_signatures.example: Places 1/4 at the midpoint of the number line

error_signatures.description: Counts marks rather than spaces (intervals)
error_signatures.example: For thirds, makes 3 marks rather than dividing into 3 equal spaces

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Fold a paper strip into equal sections. Place strip below the number line and transfer markings.

atomic_skills.title: Find equivalent fractions
atomic_skills.description: Identify and generate equivalent fractions using multiplication and division

error_signatures.description: Adds the same value to numerator and denominator rather than multiplying
error_signatures.example: Converts 1/2 to 2/3 by adding 1 to each

error_signatures.description: Does not understand equivalence means same point on number line

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use fraction walls or strips to show same length = same value. Record the multiplier used for both numerator and denominator.

levels.title: Fraction Operations
levels.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide fractions

atomic_skills.title: Add fractions with same denominator
atomic_skills.description: Add fractions by counting equal parts; simplify results

error_signatures.description: Adds numerators AND denominators

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use fraction strips. Show parts being combined; the size of parts (denominator) does not change.

atomic_skills.title: Add fractions with different denominators
atomic_skills.description: Find common denominators and add unlike fractions

error_signatures.description: Adds without finding common denominator
Finds LCD but converts only one fraction

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use fraction strips of both sizes side by side. Find the first shared length mark.

atomic_skills.title: Multiply a fraction by a whole number
atomic_skills.description: Interpret n × (a/b) as n copies of (a/b); apply and simplify

error_signatures.description: Multiplies both numerator and denominator by n

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Draw 3 copies of 2/5 on a number line. Count total fifths.

atomic_skills.title: Multiply fraction by fraction
atomic_skills.description: Apply the algorithm: (a/b) × (c/d) = ac/bd; interpret as 'fraction of a fraction'

error_signatures.description: Adds instead of multiplies
Cannot interpret as 'fraction of a fraction'
error_signatures.example: Cannot represent 2/3 of 3/4 on an area model

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use a unit square area model. Shade rows for one fraction, columns for the other. Overlap = product.

atomic_skills.title: Divide fraction by whole number
atomic_skills.description: Divide a fraction into equal parts using diagrams and the algorithm

error_signatures.description: Multiplies instead of divides

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Draw 2/3 on a number line. Split each third into 4 equal parts and identify the result.

atomic_skills.title: Divide fraction by fraction (invert and multiply)
atomic_skills.description: Apply a/b ÷ c/d = a/b × d/c and interpret with models

error_signatures.description: Inverts the wrong fraction
Cannot explain why invert-and-multiply works
error_signatures.example: Applies rule but cannot verify with a model

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use a measurement model: 'How many 4/5 fit into 2/3?' Count with a number line.

levels.title: Decimals
levels.description: Understand, compare, and operate with decimal numbers

atomic_skills.title: Understand tenths and hundredths
atomic_skills.description: Represent decimals to two places using place value and connect to fractions

error_signatures.description: Treats decimal digits as whole numbers
Cannot connect 0.3 to 3/10
error_signatures.example: Does not see tenths as a fraction

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use a decimal place value chart. Fill with base-10 blocks; connect each column to its fraction name.

atomic_skills.title: Add and subtract decimals
atomic_skills.description: Add and subtract decimal numbers using place value alignment

error_signatures.description: Misaligns decimal points
error_signatures.example: 3.4 + 0.25 written with 4 and 2 in same column

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Always write the decimal point first and align all digits to it. Use zeros as placeholders.

atomic_skills.title: Multiply and divide decimals by 10, 100, 1000
atomic_skills.description: Apply place value understanding to multiply/divide by powers of 10

error_signatures.description: Adds or removes zeros rather than moving the decimal point
Moves decimal wrong number of places

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use a place value grid. Show digits moving columns rather than the decimal moving.

atomic_skills.title: Round decimals to nearest whole or decimal place
atomic_skills.description: Apply rounding rules to decimal numbers in context

error_signatures.description: Rounds down when digit is 5
Rounds wrong digit
error_signatures.example: Rounds ones rather than tenths when rounding to 1 dp

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use a number line segment. Mark the decimal between two round numbers; identify which is closer.

levels.title: Ratio and Proportion
levels.description: Understand and apply ratio, proportion, and percentage

atomic_skills.title: Express and simplify ratios
atomic_skills.description: Write a ratio from a context and simplify using HCF

error_signatures.description: Writes ratio as fraction incorrectly
Does not simplify to lowest terms

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use bar models to represent each part of the ratio. Explicitly identify HCF before simplifying.

atomic_skills.title: Divide a quantity in a given ratio
atomic_skills.description: Share a total into parts using a ratio; find each part's value

error_signatures.description: Divides by number of terms rather than total parts
error_signatures.example: £30 in ratio 2:3: divides by 2 instead of 5

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Find total number of parts first (sum of ratio terms). Find value of 1 part. Then multiply.

atomic_skills.title: Solve proportion problems (unitary method)
atomic_skills.description: Find 1 unit then scale; apply to direct proportion contexts

error_signatures.description: Does not use unitary method; uses additive reasoning instead
error_signatures.example: If 3 items cost £12, incorrectly adds £12 to find 4 items

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Always find '1 unit' as an explicit step. Write it down before scaling.

atomic_skills.title: Calculate percentage of an amount
atomic_skills.description: Find percentages using 10% as a building block and/or decimal equivalents

error_signatures.description: Divides by percentage rather than converting to decimal
Error converting percentage to decimal

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Build from 10% (divide by 10). Then combine: 30% = 3×10%, 35% = 30%+5%.

atomic_skills.title: Calculate percentage increase and decrease
atomic_skills.description: Increase or decrease a value by a percentage; use multipliers

error_signatures.description: Finds percentage but adds to wrong original
error_signatures.example: 20% increase on £60: finds £12 but adds to £20

error_signatures.description: Cannot use multiplier method

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use bar model: whole bar = 100%. Add/remove % blocks. Then teach multiplier as one-step shortcut.

levels.title: Negative Numbers and Integers
levels.description: Extend the number system to include negative numbers; operate with integers

atomic_skills.title: Order and compare negative numbers
atomic_skills.description: Place negative numbers on a number line; compare using < and >

error_signatures.description: Thinks −5 > −2 because 5 > 2

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use a vertical thermometer. Higher on the thermometer = greater value. Negative numbers are below zero.

atomic_skills.title: Add and subtract with negative numbers
atomic_skills.description: Apply rules for adding/subtracting negative numbers on a number line

error_signatures.description: Does not understand subtracting a negative = adding
Confuses direction on number line

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use a number line with direction arrows. Subtracting reverses direction; subtracting a negative reverses twice.

atomic_skills.title: Multiply and divide with negative numbers
atomic_skills.description: Apply sign rules: same signs = positive, different signs = negative

error_signatures.description: Ignores signs and just multiplies magnitudes

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use a 2×2 sign table. Practice sign determination separately from magnitude calculation.

atomic_skills.title: Apply BODMAS/PEMDAS order of operations
atomic_skills.description: Evaluate expressions with mixed operations following correct precedence

error_signatures.description: Evaluates left to right without following precedence
Forgets to evaluate brackets first

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Circle brackets first, then underline multiplication/division, then evaluate in order.

levels.title: Algebra — Patterns and Variables
levels.description: Introduce algebraic thinking through patterns, sequences, and variable notation

atomic_skills.title: Identify and extend number patterns
atomic_skills.description: Describe the rule for a sequence and find missing terms

error_signatures.description: Identifies first difference only; misses second difference in quadratic sequences
error_signatures.example: 1,4,9,16: says 'add 3 each time' without checking differences

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Always calculate all differences. If first differences vary, calculate second differences.

atomic_skills.title: Write and evaluate algebraic expressions
atomic_skills.description: Represent unknown quantities with letters; substitute values and evaluate

error_signatures.description: Treats letter as a specific unknown number rather than a variable
Error substituting negative values
error_signatures.example: Evaluates 3x when x=−2 as 3×2=6 instead of −6

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use function machines. Input value → operation → output. Connect to expression notation.

atomic_skills.title: Simplify expressions by collecting like terms
atomic_skills.description: Group and simplify algebraic terms with the same variable

error_signatures.description: Adds unlike terms
Errors with negative coefficients when collecting

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Colour-code like terms. Collect same-colour groups before combining.

atomic_skills.title: Expand single brackets
atomic_skills.description: Multiply each term inside the bracket by the term outside

error_signatures.description: Multiplies only the first term in the bracket

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use an area model rectangle. Multiplier is the width, bracket terms are the two height sections.

atomic_skills.title: Factorise by extracting the HCF
atomic_skills.description: Find the highest common factor of terms and write in factorised form

error_signatures.description: Takes a common factor but not the highest
error_signatures.example: 6x+9: takes 3(2x+3) when HCF is 3, but only takes 3(2x+3)... actually this may be right — let me use a clearer example: 12x+8: factors as 2(6x+4) instead of 4(3x+2)

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Find HCF of numerical coefficients first. Then check if variable is common too. Verify by expanding.

levels.title: Linear Equations
levels.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities; use equations to model problems

atomic_skills.title: Solve one-step equations
atomic_skills.description: Isolate the variable in equations of the form x+a=b or ax=b

error_signatures.description: Performs inverse operation on wrong side
error_signatures.example: x+5=12: subtracts 5 from 12 only, getting x=7 correctly but by accident

error_signatures.description: Does not understand balancing (doing same to both sides)
error_signatures.example: x+5=12: crosses out +5 but does not adjust right side

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use a balance scale model. Whatever is done to one side must be done to the other.

atomic_skills.title: Solve two-step equations
atomic_skills.description: Solve equations of the form ax+b=c by applying inverse operations in order

error_signatures.description: Applies inverse operations in wrong order
error_signatures.example: 2x+3=11: divides by 2 first getting x+3=5.5 then subtracts 3

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use a function machine (forward and reverse). Reverse operations in reverse order.

tiers.title: Equations with Variables on Both Sides

atomic_skills.title: Solve equations with unknowns on both sides
atomic_skills.description: Collect variable terms on one side; constant terms on the other

error_signatures.description: Moves term incorrectly (changes to same sign rather than opposite)

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use balance model. Moving a term to the other side changes its sign. Verify each step.

atomic_skills.title: Form and solve equations from word problems
atomic_skills.description: Translate a word problem into an equation; solve and interpret in context

error_signatures.description: Writes equation with digits and words mixed; cannot form clean algebraic equation
error_signatures.example: 'Three more than double a number is 11' written as 3+2=11

error_signatures.description: Solves equation correctly but does not answer the question in context
error_signatures.example: Finds x=4 but problem asked for the original number which was x+2=6

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Define the variable first. Write in full: 'Let x = ...' before forming the equation.

levels.title: Geometry — Shape and Space
levels.description: Properties of shapes, angles, area, and volume

atomic_skills.title: Identify and measure angles
atomic_skills.description: Classify angles (acute, right, obtuse, reflex); measure with a protractor

error_signatures.description: Reads wrong scale on protractor
Does not align protractor baseline with arm of angle

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Check: Does the angle look acute or obtuse? Use this to select the correct scale reading.

atomic_skills.title: Angle relationships (supplementary, vertically opposite, angles in triangle)
atomic_skills.description: Apply angle rules to find unknown angles in diagrams

error_signatures.description: Cannot identify which angle rule applies
error_signatures.example: Uses co-interior angles rule when corresponding angles are needed

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Label angle relationships explicitly before calculating. State the rule in words first.

atomic_skills.title: Calculate area of rectangles and triangles
atomic_skills.description: Apply formulas: rectangle A=lw; triangle A=½bh

error_signatures.description: Confuses area and perimeter
error_signatures.example: Adds sides when area is asked; multiplies when perimeter is asked

error_signatures.description: Does not halve when finding triangle area
error_signatures.example: A = b × h instead of ½ × b × h

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Count squares to verify formula. Pair triangle with its rectangle to show it is exactly half.

atomic_skills.title: Calculate volume of cuboids
atomic_skills.description: Apply V = l × w × h; identify dimensions from diagrams

error_signatures.description: Multiplies only two dimensions (area instead of volume)

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use cubic centimetre blocks. Build the base layer (l×w) then stack h layers. Count total.

levels.title: Statistics and Data
levels.description: Collect, represent, and interpret data; calculate averages

atomic_skills.title: Calculate mean, median, and mode
atomic_skills.description: Find each average and understand when each is appropriate

error_signatures.description: Calculates mean as sum rather than sum ÷ n
Does not sort data before finding median
error_signatures.example: Median of 3,7,1,5 taken as second value (7) instead of sorting first

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Use acronym: Mode = Most frequent; Median = Middle (must sort); Mean = shared evenly.

atomic_skills.title: Interpret and draw bar charts and pie charts
atomic_skills.description: Read scales accurately; calculate angles for pie charts; draw with appropriate labels

error_signatures.description: Misreads scale intervals on bar chart
error_signatures.example: Scale in 5s: reads a bar reaching between marks as 5 rather than 7.5

error_signatures.description: Incorrect pie chart angle calculation
error_signatures.example: Divides frequency by 360 instead of by total then multiplies by 360

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: For pie charts: fraction of total × 360 = angle. Always verify angles sum to 360°.

atomic_skills.title: Calculate and express probability
atomic_skills.description: Express probability as a fraction, decimal, and percentage; use sample space

error_signatures.description: Uses impossible/certain language but cannot quantify
error_signatures.example: Knows probability is between 0 and 1 but cannot calculate P(event)

error_signatures.description: Does not list complete sample space
error_signatures.example: Counts favourable outcomes only, not total outcomes

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Always list all possible outcomes (sample space) before counting favourable outcomes.

levels.title: Advanced Problem Solving
levels.description: Apply multi-step reasoning and connect mathematical ideas across topics

atomic_skills.title: Solve multi-step word problems
atomic_skills.description: Plan and execute a multi-step solution; check reasonableness at each step

error_signatures.description: Loses track of the question mid-solution
error_signatures.example: Performs correct calculations but answers a sub-question rather than the final question

error_signatures.description: Cannot identify which operations are needed
error_signatures.example: Uses addition when the problem requires multiplication then subtraction

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Identify: What do I know? What do I need to find? What intermediate steps are needed? Draw a diagram.

atomic_skills.title: Use and justify mathematical conjectures
atomic_skills.description: Test a conjecture with examples; explain why a generalisation is or is not valid

error_signatures.description: Cannot distinguish between showing and proving
error_signatures.example: Tests two cases and claims proved for all cases

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Distinguish: examples support a conjecture but a counterexample disproves it. One counterexample is enough.

atomic_skills.title: Apply systematic problem-solving strategies
atomic_skills.description: Use drawing, working backwards, trial and improvement, or algebraic methods to solve non-routine problems

error_signatures.description: Uses trial and error unsystematically
error_signatures.example: Tries random values without narrowing the search space

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Teach Polya's steps explicitly: Understand → Plan → Execute → Review. Revisit the plan when stuck.

levels.title: Quadratic Algebra
levels.description: Factorise and work with quadratic expressions of the form x² + bx + c

atomic_skills.title: Factorise quadratic expressions of the form x² + bx + c
atomic_skills.description: Find two binomial factors by identifying a pair of numbers that multiply to c and add to b

error_signatures.description: Chooses factors with wrong signs
Correct sign but wrong pair of numbers

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: List factor pairs of c. Check which pair adds to b. Then assign signs to satisfy the sum.

levels.title: Functions and Straight Lines
levels.description: Interpret and work with linear functions in the form y = mx + c

atomic_skills.title: Identify gradient, x-intercept and y-intercept of a linear function
atomic_skills.description: For y = mx + c: identify gradient m, y-intercept by setting x=0, x-intercept by setting y=0

error_signatures.description: Swaps x-intercept and y-intercept
error_signatures.example: For y = 2x - 4 gives y-int: 2 instead of -4

error_signatures.description: Drops the sign of the gradient
error_signatures.example: For y = -3x + 1 gives gradient: 3 instead of -3

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: y-intercept: substitute x=0 and solve. x-intercept: substitute y=0 and solve. Gradient is the coefficient of x including its sign.

levels.title: Exponentials and Logarithms
levels.description: Convert between exponential and logarithmic notation and evaluate expressions

atomic_skills.title: Convert between exponential and logarithmic form
atomic_skills.description: Apply the definition log_b(x) = n ↔ b^n = x to evaluate and convert expressions

error_signatures.description: Confuses base and argument in the log
error_signatures.example: log₂(8) = 2 instead of 3 (confuses base with answer)

error_signatures.description: Applies log rules to exponential or vice versa

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Write log_b(x) = n as b^n = x. Ask: what power do I raise b to, to get x?

levels.title: Trigonometric Ratios
levels.description: Apply SOH CAH TOA to find sine, cosine and tangent in right-angled triangles

atomic_skills.title: Find sine, cosine and tangent using SOH CAH TOA
atomic_skills.description: Identify opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse relative to a given angle; compute the three trig ratios

error_signatures.description: Swaps opposite and adjacent
error_signatures.example: Uses adjacent/hypotenuse for sine instead of opposite/hypotenuse

error_signatures.description: Inverts the ratio (flips numerator and denominator)
error_signatures.example: sin θ = hypotenuse/opposite instead of opposite/hypotenuse

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Label the triangle first: H=hypotenuse (longest), O=opposite the angle, A=adjacent. Then SOH: sin=O/H, CAH: cos=A/H, TOA: tan=O/A.

levels.title: Calculus — Differentiation
levels.description: Differentiate polynomial functions using the power rule

atomic_skills.title: Differentiate polynomial functions using the power rule
atomic_skills.description: Apply d/dx(axⁿ) = naxⁿ⁻¹ to each term; differentiate sums and differences of power functions

error_signatures.description: Multiplies by the power but forgets to reduce it by 1
Drops or miscalculates the new coefficient after multiplying

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: For each term axⁿ: new coefficient = n×a, new power = n-1. Constants differentiate to 0.
